Hi Rosa, this is Diego Ferraz from the mining account. It is Tuesday, about ten in the morning, and I am sorry to leave three things on a voicemail. First, our finance director wants to know whether the new fare includes two bags or only one, because the team always travels with equipment. Second, could you tell me when the contract will be ready? Our legal department asks me about it every single day. And third, please do not send another reminder about the March invoice. It was paid on Friday, and I have the confirmation here in front of me. Call me back before noon on Thursday if you can, because after that I am on a plane to Santiago.

When a client leaves you a question, your job is not only to answer it. It is to pass it on so precisely that a colleague could answer it without calling the client again. That means keeping the question as a question. Not Diego called about the bags, but Diego asked whether the new fare included two bags. Requests work in exactly the same way. If somebody asked you to do something, write down who asked, what they asked for, and by when. And if somebody told you not to do something, write that down first, because it is the message your colleague is most likely to get wrong. Finally, reply on the same day, even when you do not have the answer yet. A short message that acknowledges the request and gives a date is professional. Silence is not.
